title: Decisions and fixes after PRJ-05 (visible behavior changes)
statusScope: The five decisions the project owner took after PRJ-05 are implemented as stated. Unlike PRJ-01 to PRJ-05 this phase changes behavior on purpose, in exactly three places; everything else is still identical to the original upload. Verification is the same fake-DB differential plus scratch-copy typecheck/build/tests; the repo's frozen install still fails and no real database or browser was used.
request: Project owner: '1-5 fix as you recommend, 1 fix and the other you recommend'. Interpreted as: #1 fix; #2 to #4 follow the recommendation; #5 fix (recommended). #6 and #7 were not requested and are untouched.

decisions.how: handler registered before GET /projects/:id/enrolled-entities; frozen route surface re-baselined; knownShadowedRoutes emptied; validator fails on any unexplained shadow
decisions.visibleChange: the endpoint now returns the grouped entity list instead of 400 'Invalid project id'
decisions.consumerCheck: artifacts/ayzen/src/pages/user/vault-enrollment-entity.tsx declares an EnrolledEntity type that matches the handler output field for field (checked by reading the types; UI not run)

decisions.why: teams.ts: a leader enrolls the whole team using the leader's own vault entity, written into each member's row; bulk.ts: many of the caller's own entities with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Distinct features, not copies of the single enroll flow.
decisions.openObservation: Neither charges credits while single enroll does. Not decided: may be intended or a billing gap.

decisions.why: Unifying would add a broadcast and Telegram alert it does not have today.

decisions.action: KEPT raw sums with the '$' label
decisions.why: Converting would change public receipt numbers; current behavior is pinned by tests.

fixes.was: deadline (POST and PATCH /projects) and startedAt (PATCH) were interpolated into raw SQL without escaping; admin/moderator callers could inject SQL.
fixes.now: they pass through the same esc() as every other raw field.
fixes.proof: UPDATE projects SET started_at = '2026-04-04' OR '1'='1' became started_at = '2026-04-04'' OR ''1''=''1'; valid dates generate byte-identical SQL (checked in unit tests and in 3 whole-file scenarios that stayed identical).
fixes.limit: Escaping neutralizes injection; it does not validate that the value is a date, so a malformed date still fails at the database cast as before.

fixes.was: status validated by indexing a plain object, so toString/constructor/hasOwnProperty were accepted and stored as the enrollment status.
fixes.now: own-property check on a string; inherited keys and non-strings get the existing 400.
fixes.proof: whole-file scenarios 'status prototype key toString/constructor': original 200 and stored the status, now 400.
